DAMGHANI:v1p237/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r2.claim: Saʿy can mean moving quickly or hurrying.
DAMGHANI:v1p237/r2.anchor: يعني يسرع نظيرها في سورة يس

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r1.claim: The word yasʿā means to act zealously, not necessarily to run; in 62:9 it means turning eagerly to God’s word, like a thirsty person approaching a fountain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r1.anchor: means to do something with zeal and enthusiasm

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.claim: The indifferent are absorbed in worldly pleasures and do not consider the afterlife, whereas those who fear meeting God are receptive; the Prophet pursued the former while neglecting the latter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2.anchor: there are people who fear meeting God in the Hereafter

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

SAMIN-DURR:80:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:8/r1.claim: يسعى is a circumstantial clause for the subject of جاءك; وهو يخشى is another circumstance for the subject of يسعى, a circumstance within a circumstance. Treating it as a second coordinated circumstance is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:80:8/r1.anchor: يسعى }: حال من فاعل " جاءك " وقوله " وهو يخشى " جملة حالية من فاعل " يسعى " ، فهو حال من حال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r10.claim: The man who comes striving is hurrying in pursuit of his religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r10.anchor: وأما من جاءك يسعى: أي يمشي بسرعة في أمر دينه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p41#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41#2/r1.claim: He comes hastening, seeking from the Prophet guidance's rulings and qualities of good.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p41#2/r1.anchor: أي حال كونه مسرعا طالبا لما عندك من أحكام الرشد وخصال الخير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r5.claim: The poor seeker comes quickly, eager for the good and reminder of God that the Prophet offers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r5.anchor: أي مسرعا رغبة فيما عندك من الخير المذكر بالله وهو فقير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r7.claim: The seeker’s arrival and fear contrast with the rich man’s failure to come and lack of fear, warning against favoring the wealthy and slighting a sincere visitor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r7.anchor: وذكر المجيء والخسية ثانيا يدل على ضدهما أولا , وسر ذلك التحذير مما يدعو إليه الطبع البشري من الميل إلى الأغنياء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r8.claim: The verbal form depicts someone coming urgently and seeking good; a person who approaches and presses through the crowd to reach the Prophet has a great claim on him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r8.anchor: وإلى أن من يقصد الانسان ويتخطى رقاب الناس إليه له عليك حق عظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.claim: The passage uses ḥtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor second, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first case.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الغنى أولا يدل على الفقر ثانيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r10.claim: The Prophet’s slight distraction from the sincere seeker for elite prospects cannot benefit the religion as much as the seeker’s evident readiness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r10.anchor: وفي التعبير بذلك إشارة إلى أن الاشتغال بأولئك لا فائدة فيه على ما تفهمه تصاريف المادة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r11.claim: The dropped tā in the verb indicates that the distraction is slight.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r11.anchor: تشاغلا حفيفا بما أشار إليه حذف التاء

DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.claim: In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مجلس من ناس من وجوه قريش منهم أبو جهل بن هشام وعتبة بن ربيعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r13.claim: يسعى can mean walking, or striving in one's affairs, religious practice, and approach to the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r13.anchor: أي يمشي، وقيل المعنى: يسعى في شؤونه وأمر دينه وتقربه منك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r21.claim: The immediate context concerns Quraysh's disbelievers and Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, but the lesson also applies to anyone sharing their qualities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r21.anchor: فالسبب ما ذكر من كفار قريش وعبد الله بن أم مكتوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r22.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r22.claim: People of religious learning are instructed to bring near the righteous weak and prefer them over socially noble people lacking goodness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r22.anchor: فحمله الشرع والعلم مخاطبون في تقريب الضعيف من أهل الخير وتقديمه على الشريف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#2/r1.claim: The first of two views takes yasʿa to mean that he walks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#2/r1.anchor: وأما من جاءك يسعى ﴾ فيه قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#3/r1.claim: The second view says his striving means doing good; this is Ibn Umm Maktum, who fears God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#3/r1.anchor: والثاني يعمل في الخير وهو ابن أم مكتوم وهو يخشى الله

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.claim: They say it was revealed when Ibn Umm Maktūm interrupted the Prophet's effort to convert Meccan leaders; the Prophet turned back to them and God rebuked him.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم أتى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored him, welcomed him as the man over whom his Lord reproached him, and asked his needs.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5.anchor: فكان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعد ذلك يكرمه، وإذا رآه قال: مرحبا بمن عاتبني ربي فيه،

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.speaker: أنس
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.claim: Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya in armor with a black banner.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6.anchor: قال أنس: رأيته يوم القادسية، عليه درع، ومعه راية سوداء.

JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd relates the saying that if the Messenger concealed revelation, he would have concealed this passage.
JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان يقال: لو كتم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - شيئا من الوحي لكتم هذا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r19.claim: Yasʿā means that the poor man hastens in seeking good.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#6/r1.claim: The man hurries to the Prophet in pursuit of good.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#6/r1.anchor: ﴿ وأما من جاءك يسعى ﴾ يسرع فى طلب الخير

BURSEVI:v10p259/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259/r1.claim: The seeker comes quickly, eager for the guidance, religious rulings, and good qualities available from the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r1.anchor: أي حال كونه مسرعا طالبا لما عندك من أحكام الرشد وخصال الخير

BURSEVI:v10p259/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r3.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v10p259/r3.claim: Saʿdī al-Muftī sees an ellipsis by ihtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first clause.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r3.anchor: ذكر الغنى أولا للدلالة على الفقر ثانيا والمجيء والخشية ثانيا للدلالة على ضدهما أولا

BURSEVI:v10p259/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259/r9.claim: The account teaches that worth lies in souls and spiritual states, not outward appearance or wealth: faith makes the socially lowly noble, while unbelief makes the socially esteemed wretched.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r9.anchor: حيث أفادت القصة أن العبرة بالأرواح والأحوال لا بالأشباح والأموال والعزيز من أعزه الله بالإيمان والطاعة

BURSEVI:v10p259/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259/r10.claim: A report says the Prophet thereafter never frowned at a poor person or sought out a rich one, and the poor held an honored place in his gathering.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r10.anchor: روى إنه عليه السلام ما بعس بعد ذلك في وجه ففير قط ولا تصدى لغني وكان الفقراء في مجلسه

BURSEVI:v10p259/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259/r11.claim: The episode instructs scholars, judges, and rulers to draw a weak seeker of good near and prefer him over a prominent person lacking good.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r11.anchor: فحملة الشرع والعلم والحكام مخاطبون في تقريب الضعيف من أهل الخير وتقديمه على الشريف العاري عن الخير

BURSEVI:v10p259/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r12.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p259/r12.claim: Some say the passage honors poverty and its people while devaluing worldly status; companionship with sincere, detached poor people benefits, unlike companionship with the rich.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r12.anchor: بين الله درجة الفقر وتعظيم أهله وخسة الدنيا وتحقير أهلها

BURSEVI:v10p259/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r13.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v10p259/r13.claim: A hadith says that favoring a rich person by treating a poor person unjustly destroys a third of one’s religion.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r13.anchor: من تحامل على فقير لغني فقد هدم ثلث دينه

BURSEVI:v10p259/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259/r14.claim: Taḥāmala can mean enduring something with difficulty, or treating another person unjustly.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r14.anchor: تحاملت على الشيء إذا تكلفت الشيء على مشقة وتحامل فلان على فلان إذا لم يعدل

BURSEVI:v10p259/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r15.speaker: بعض الأكابر
BURSEVI:v10p259/r15.claim: Some great Sufis explain that the Prophet honored Quraysh’s chiefs as manifestations of divine majesty, while a higher station is to see no distinction among people under God’s absolute reality.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r15.anchor: وقال بعض الأكابر إنما كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يتواضع لأكابر قريش لأن الأعزاء من الخلائق مظهر لعزة الإلهية

BURSEVI:v10p259/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259/r16.claim: The higher instruction is to remain with those who call on God morning and evening, as stated later in the Quran.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r16.anchor: وهو ما أمره الله به آخرا بعدما صدر سورة عبس في قوله واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشى

BURSEVI:v10p259/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259/r17.speaker: الله تعالى
BURSEVI:v10p259/r17.claim: Bursevi invokes the divine saying about the hungry and thirsty person whom people failed to feed and give drink.
BURSEVI:v10p259/r17.anchor: كما قال جعت فلم تطعمني وظمئت فلم تسقني الحديث كم افي الجواهر للشعراني

RAZI-FULL:v31p52#5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#5/r1.claim: Yasʿā means that the man hastens in seeking good, as in the command to hasten to Friday prayer, 62:9.
RAZI-FULL:v31p52#5/r1.anchor: أن يسرع في طلب الخير ، كقوله : { فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله }

TABRISI:80:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r6.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, also named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿa al-Fihri, when he came as the Prophet was urging Quraysh leaders toward Islam.
TABRISI:80:20/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك ابن ربيعة الفهري

TABRISI:80:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20/r7.claim: The Prophet was speaking with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; the Prophet turned away, thinking the leaders might scorn a following of blind people and slaves.
TABRISI:80:20/r7.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يناجي عتبة بن ربيعة وأبا جهل بن هشام والعباس بن عبد المطلب وأبيا وأمية ابني خلف

TABRISI:80:20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:80:20/r8.claim: Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him deputy in Medina twice.
TABRISI:80:20/r8.anchor: وكان رسول الله بعد ذلك يكرمه

TABRISI:80:20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:80:20/r9.claim: Anas ibn Malik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black standard.
TABRISI:80:20/r9.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: فرأيته يوم القادسية وعليه درع ومعه راية سوداء

TABRISI:80:20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r10.speaker: المرتضى علم الهدى
TABRISI:80:20/r10.claim: Al-Murtada rejects identifying the passage's subject as the Prophet: the text does not name him, and frowning at a believing seeker or preferring rich people to the poor conflicts with his noble character.
TABRISI:80:20/r10.anchor: قال المرتضى علم الهدى قدس الله روحه: ليس في ظاهر الآية دلالة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213#2/r1.claim: He rejects the suggestion that the Prophet turned toward the wealthy for their riches: the verse says the other man came striving and fearing, not that he was poor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213#2/r1.anchor: وهو فاسد- هاهنا- لأن إقبال النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- لم يكن لثروتهم ومالهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p215#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p215#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، والكلبي، ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p215#2/r1.claim: They understand the man's striving as seeking God's pleasure and doing good that pleases Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p215#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والكلبي، ومقاتل (¬5): يسعى في الطلب لرضاء الله، والعمل في الخير وما يرضي الله

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.claim: The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائمه الخطاب في قوله بعد { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى }

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.claim: The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5.anchor: أنك تعتني وتقبل على من استغنى واستكبر عن اتباع الحق وما عليك أن لا يزكى وتتلهى وتعرض عمن يجتهد في التزكي وهو يخشى

TABATABAI:80:5-12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r9.claim: Saʿy literally means walking quickly; in context the man comes hastening to remember and purify himself through religious learning.
TABATABAI:80:5-12/r9.anchor: السعي الإسراع في المشي فمعنى قوله { وأما من جاءك يسعى } بحسب ما يفيده المقام

TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r13.claim: The man who comes eagerly, strives for good, and fears God is Ibn Umm Maktum.
TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r13.anchor: أي يعمل في الخير يعني ابن أم مكتوم

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r14.claim: The man who comes eagerly to seek knowledge and fears God is neglected while the Prophet turns elsewhere and occupies himself with others.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r14.anchor: يسعى } . لطلب العلم ، ويخشى الله فأنت عنه تتلهى

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.claim: The whole passage is a reproach directed to the Prophet on behalf of the poor.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15.anchor: وهذا كله من قبيل العتاب معه لأجل الفقراء

NAHHAS:v5p149/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p149/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p149/r14.claim: The verbal clauses at verses 8 and 9 can be circumstantial accusatives; the latter clause may also be another predicate.
NAHHAS:v5p149/r14.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال وكذا 9 ويجوز أن تكون الجملة خبرا آخر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.claim: ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1.anchor: There is no basic difference between the central theme of both sūrahs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r9.claim: The person who comes hastening is Ibn Umm Maktum.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r11.claim: This is the person who comes swiftly seeking good.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects this opening to the prior calls to heed and fear: humble people whom the world overlooks are especially cared for and chosen by God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما قال سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.claim: The saying that a disheveled, dusty person whom people ignore could swear an oath that God would fulfill illustrates the hidden rank of the humble.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2.anchor: إجابة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأعلى منزلته لديه ( رب أشعث أغبر لا يؤبه له لو أقسم على الله لأبره )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.claim: Ibn Umm Maktūm was the Prophet’s muezzin and the man whose visit occasioned the sūra’s admonition.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3.anchor: ومنهم ابن مكتوب الأعمى مؤذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الذي بسببه نزلت السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.claim: The rebuke teaches the Prophet to remain patiently with people like Ibn Maktūm and not to despise them, echoing other admonitions and the command not to drive away those who seek God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4.anchor: وتنبيها على أن يعمل نفسه الكريمة على مصابرة أمثال ابن مكتوم وأن لا يحتقر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.claim: Ibn Maktūm sought instruction while the Prophet addressed a Quraysh notable whose conversion he hoped would save the man and his kin; attending to that hope led him to neglect the immediate visitor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5.anchor: لما دخل عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن أم مكتون سائلا ومسترشدا وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم يكلم رجلا من أشراف قريش

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.claim: The description of the Prophet as a warner to those who fear applies to Ibn Umm Maktūm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2.anchor: كابن أم مكتوم , من نمط ما نزل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.claim: The command to keep company with those who call upon God morning and evening is another passage revealed in the pattern of Ibn Umm Maktūm’s case.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3.anchor: نمط ما نزل في ابن أم مكتوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r10.claim: The clause about the one who comes is coordinated with the self-sufficient person as the opposing side, completing the division by contrasting opposites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r10.anchor: عطف على جملة { أما من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) اقتضى ذكره قصد المقابلة مع المعطوف عليها مقابلة الضدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r11.claim: The one who comes eagerly is Ibn Umm Maktūm, confirming the account in the opening verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r11.anchor: هو ابن أم مكتوم ، فحصل بمضمون هذه الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r12.claim: Saʿy is brisk walking, used for eagerness to meet; it contrasts with the self-sufficient person’s aversion to receiving the Prophet’s attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r12.anchor: والسعي : شدة المشي ، كني به عن الحرص على اللقاء فهو مقابل لحال من استغنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r10.claim: This clause contrasts with verse 5 and completes the division by setting opposites against each other; it also reinforces the opening account of the blind man’s visit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r10.anchor: عطف على جملة { أما من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) اقتضى ذكره قصد المقابلة مع المعطوف عليها مقابلة الضدين إتماما للتقسيم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r11.claim: The man who comes eagerly is Ibn Umm Maktūm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r11.anchor: والمراد : بمن جاء يسعى : هو ابن أم مكتوم ، فحصل بمضمون هذه الجملة تأكيد لمضمون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r12.claim: Saʿy is brisk walking, used here for eagerness to meet the Prophet; this contrasts with the self-sufficient man’s disdain for being approached.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r12.anchor: والسعي : شدة المشي ، كني به عن الحرص على اللقاء فهو مقابل لحال من استغنى لأن استغناءه استغناء الممتعض من التصدي له .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r4.claim: The blind man came purposefully and feared God, seeking guidance from what the Prophet taught, but the Prophet was occupied with another person.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r4.anchor: ويؤمك ليهتدي بما تقول له، (فأنت عنه تلهى) أي: تتشاغل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.claim: God directs the Prophet to warn everyone equally, without favoring the eminent over the weak, rich over poor, masters over slaves, men over women, or adults over children; God guides whom He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5.anchor: ومن هاهنا أمر الله عز وجل رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا يخص بالإنذار أحدا، بل يساوي فيه بين الشريف والضعيف، والفقير والغني، والسادة والعبيد،

MUQATIL:80:8-17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r1.claim: The person who comes striving in the heat and fears God is Ibn Umm Maktūm.
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r1.anchor: في الحر { وهو يخشى } [آية: 9] الله يعني بن أم مكتوم

MUQATIL:80:8-17/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r3.claim: God admonishes the Prophet to stop attending to those who feel self-sufficient and to welcome, rather than turn from, the person who comes fearing his Lord.
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r3.anchor: لا تقبل عليه ولا تعرض عن من جاءك يسعى، ولا تقبل على من استغنى وتعرض عن من يخشى ربه

MUQATIL:80:8-17/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r4.claim: After the revelation concerning Ibn Umm Maktūm, the Prophet honored him and appointed him deputy over Medina twice during military expeditions.
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r4.anchor: أكرمه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واستخلفه بعد ذلك على المدينة مرتين في غزواته

QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r9.claim: The person who comes eagerly is seeking knowledge for God's sake.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأما من جآءك يسعى } يطلب العلم لله
